inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 tanshin statement of changes in equity, 'Share-based payment' 475 (FY2024: 426); no equity-award taxes disclosed. SBC is 0.04% of revenue -- an SBC-zero market; house and street bases coincide.
inputs.share_count_basis: Company-published diluted count at H1 FY2026 (157.723M; diluted EPS 460.16 on 72,578 attributable). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows (0.04% of revenue) and buybacks (FY2024 3.9bn, FY2025 6.0bn, H1 FY2026 nil) are value-neutral in the house method -- they are the mechanism that keeps the count flat, not an extra source of value.
inputs.net_debt_basis: H1 FY2026 bonds and borrowings 238,253 current + 376,969 non-current = 615,222, less cash and cash equivalents 147,059. Lease liabilities EXCLUDED (they sit inside 'other financial liabilities' 81,891 and are charged in the flows instead -- see lease_treatment). The 55.2bn proceeds from the H1 asset sale are already inside June cash.
inputs.wacc_rationale: JPY-built. Risk-free ~1.7% (10y JGB, 2026), ERP 6%, beta ~1.1 -> cost of equity ~8.3%; after-tax cost of debt ~1.1% (FY2025 interest expense 8,535 on ~535bn = 1.6% pre-tax); market-value weights ~62/38 give a textbook WACC near 5.7%. House uses 7.5%: a JPY rate that assumes BoJ normalisation continues (JGB 10y toward 2.5%) and does not lean on today's unusually cheap yen debt in perpetuity. Same WACC in all three scenarios -- cyclicality, tariffs and FX are charged in the scenario flows, not stacked on the discount rate (adaptations (f)). Terminal cap 13x owner FCF (12-14x across scenarios) is below the Gordon value at 7.5%/2% (18.5x) and binds; a tyre maker does not exit at 18x FCF.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost. IFRS 16 filer: lease principal 9,751 (FY2025 financing CF) plus an estimated ~0.5bn lease interest = ~10.3bn = 0.83% of revenue, charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path (0.85%). Lease liabilities are therefore excluded from net debt. Cash-tax EBIT uses D&A ex right-of-use depreciation: segment-table D&A 64,102 (5.2% of FY2025 revenue) rather than the cash-flow 73,622 (6.0%), the 9.5bn gap matching lease principal.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated; NCI deducted once in the equity bridge at H1 FY2026 book (9,041). NCI profit share is ~0.6% of profit (441 of 73,019 in H1 FY2026), so attributable-only flows would differ by noise.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component route, 10-year horizon (capex 9% of revenue is a supercycle -- Mexico PCR plant, India OTR plant, China -- and the owner-FCF margin only matures once capex normalises toward D&A around year 6-8). Routed via dcf-methods: normal operating company, Japanese cyclical industrial, so owner-fcf.md plus the adaptations file (currency, leases, NCI, SBC-zero, risk-once). First valuation of this ticker; no prior model. Revenue base FY2025 1,234,959; year 1 = FY2026 at guidance +6.9% (1,320,000, raised three times since the Feb-2024 initial 1,150,000). EBITDA margin is anchored to BUSINESS PROFIT, not operating profit: FY2026 guided OP 199.5bn exceeds BP 192.5bn only because of the 36.2bn H1 gain on sale of non-current assets, which also inflates the 117bn net-income / 744 EPS guidance; the model haircuts BP-EBITDA by ~0.6-0.7% of revenue for the recurring 'other expenses' (impairment, restructuring: -1.1% FY2025, -1.4% FY2024). Interest income (4,380 FY2025) is NOT stripped: the company is net debt 468bn, so there is no cash pile being double-counted; finance income sits below BP and is already outside the flows, and its source assets (non-current other financial assets 49,647 at book, composition not broken out in the tanshin) are added in the bridge under the matching-asset rule and flagged as unverified. Owner FCF after also deducting lease principal would be 13,120 on FY2025; the 22,871 last_fcf follows the contract formula (reported 23,346 - SBC 475). Cash conversion is the thesis-defining weakness: FY2025 NI 105.4bn converted to FCF of 23.3bn after 112bn capex and ~40bn of working-capital build; NWC (receivables + inventories - payables) is ~44% of revenue, so growth consumes cash (wc_capture negative). Cash tax 32% = FY2025 ETR (50.3bn on 157.2bn PBT); FY2025 cash taxes paid 57.1bn and H1 FY2026 71.1bn ran above book because of timing on the FY2025 bill (income taxes payable fell 53.9 -> 38.4bn), not a structurally higher rate. SBC kept explicit at 0.04%; band collapses to a point. Goodwill 340bn (ATG 2016, Trelleborg Wheel Systems 2023, Goodyear OTR Feb-2025) is 30% of equity -- impairment risk is a bear axis, not in the flows.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: FY2026 guidance +6.9% fading to GDP-plus tyre demand (~4% average over FY2027-FY2030); the equity and revenue CAGRs are acquisition- (TWS 2023, G-OTR 2025) and yen-weakness-inflated and are not a forward run-rate
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 19.9% and revenue 17.5% against an owner-FCF 5yr CAGR of -13.4% (FY2020 46,903 -> FY2025 22,871; 3yr n/a from a negative FY2022 base). The reported growth has been paid for with debt-funded acquisitions, 112bn of capex and working-capital build, not with cash to shareholders.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs on FY2020->FY2025 (5yr) and FY2022->FY2025 (3yr), December year-ends, from the Metrics CSV. FCF series is owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC; interest income not stripped, net-debt company). EPS is on today's share basis throughout (2015 2-for-1 consolidation already restated).

base.narrative: FY2026 at guidance (revenue +6.9%, BP 192.5bn -> BP-EBITDA ~20.9% less 0.7% other-expense haircut). Growth fades from 4.5% to 2.5% as the Mexico/India/China plants ramp into GDP-plus tyre demand. EBITDA margin eases to 19.0% mid-cycle -- 1pp below the FY2026 peak, 2pp above the FY2021-25 average of ~17%, crediting the structural OHT mix (ATG + TWS + G-OTR) but not the current pricing/raw-material tailwind. Capex 9% -> 6.5% over 8 years as the plant programme completes; D&A ex-ROU rises 5.3% -> 6.0% behind it. NWC absorbs 40% of each yen of revenue growth (balance-sheet ratio ~44%, modest efficiency gain). Cash tax 32% = FY2025 ETR.

bull.narrative: YX2029 delivered: a fourth guidance beat in FY2026 (H1 beat plan by 20.8bn of BP), the new plants fill on schedule, OHT ag demand recovers from the grain-price trough and G-OTR mining tyres hold pricing; the yen stays weak (USD/JPY ~155+), tariffs are passed through. EBITDA margin expands to 21.5% (BP margin ~15.5%, still below the deck's 17% ambition). Working-capital discipline improves to 35% capture. Terminal cap 14x, g 2.5%.

bear.narrative: H1 FY2026 is the peak. H2 slows (guidance already implies H2 BP margin 14.2% vs 15.0% in H1), then FY2027 revenue is flat as the yen strengthens toward 130-140, US tariffs on imported tyres bite the Japan/Asia-sourced volume, natural-rubber and carbon-black costs rise ahead of pricing, and OHT ag demand stays depressed. EBITDA margin reverts to 16.0% -- the FY2023-24 level, pre the FY2025 price/mix uplift -- and the new plants ramp into soft demand. Capex is cut faster but NWC capture worsens to 45%. Goodwill impairment on TWS/G-OTR would be non-cash and is not in the flows. Terminal cap 12x, g 1.5%.

scenario_narratives.base: Yokohama's axes are (1) the OHT cycle -- agricultural and OTR tyres via ATG, Trelleborg Wheel Systems and the Feb-2025 Goodyear OTR deal are now ~30% of tyre revenue at above-group margins, and ag demand tracks grain prices; (2) US tariffs and USD/JPY (guidance assumes 156), both of which move the yen P&L of a company with most of its sales outside Japan; (3) raw-material cost versus pricing power in consumer tyres (the ADVAN/GEOLANDAR premium mix); (4) a capex supercycle (9% of revenue: Mexico PCR, India OTR, China) and working capital that absorbs ~40% of revenue growth, which is why FY2025 net income of 105bn became FCF of 23bn; and (5) a balance sheet carrying 468bn net debt and 340bn of acquisition goodwill. Base: guidance for FY2026, GDP-plus growth after, margin eases 1pp to a mid-cycle 19% EBITDA, capex normalises by FY2033.
scenario_narratives.bull: YX2029 lands: plants fill, OHT ag recovers, G-OTR integration delivers synergies, yen stays weak and tariffs are priced through. EBITDA margin 21.5%, growth 5-6% for four years, better working-capital discipline. Dividend payout rises from 30% toward the 40-50% the YX2029 capital-allocation page sketches.
scenario_narratives.bear: Peak-cycle earnings. Yen appreciation, tariffs on Asia-sourced volume, raw-material inflation and a prolonged ag downturn drop EBITDA margin back to 16% (FY2023-24 level) on flat FY2027 revenue. New-plant depreciation and interest on 615bn of gross debt (already up 8.5bn/yr) then land on a smaller profit base; goodwill impairment is the headline risk.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: a cyclical with 468bn net debt, 340bn of acquisition goodwill, tariff and USD/JPY exposure, and H1 FY2026 margins at an all-time high is more exposed to a reversion than the default assumes. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things -- plant ramps on schedule, an OHT ag recovery and a persistently weak yen -- to coincide. Base 50% carries management's thrice-raised FY2026 guidance, which has a strong recent record.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the tyre business as a stream of owner FCF after the capex programme and working-capital build that the headline P/E (~9x FY2025) ignores. Business profit, not operating profit or net income, is the anchor because FY2026 reported figures carry a 36bn one-off disposal gain. Risk is charged once, in three probability-weighted scenarios with the same JPY WACC; leases are an operating cost and lease liabilities are not debt; NCI and the non-operating financial assets are bridged once each.
key_risks_to_valuation: Working-capital capture (-40% of revenue growth) and the capex glide (9% -> 6.5%) are the two drivers that convert a 9x P/E into a modest FCF yield; both are judgments on a company that has never shown sustained free-cash conversion at its current scale.
Terminal cap 13x owner FCF binds (Gordon at 7.5%/2% would be 18.5x); the value is sensitive to the cap, not to terminal growth.
USD/JPY: guidance assumes 156; a return to 130-140 removes several points of yen-denominated margin, and the model has no explicit FX driver beyond the bear margin path.
Goodwill of 340bn (30% of equity) on three OHT acquisitions; an impairment would not touch the flows but would mark the acquisitions as overpaid.
Non-current other financial assets (49.6bn) are bridged at book without a yuho breakdown; if they are mostly operating loans/deposits rather than securities the bridge is ~315/share too generous.
FY2026 EPS guidance (744) and H1 net profit (72.6bn) include a 36.2bn pre-tax disposal gain; screens built on reported EPS will overstate the run-rate by ~15%.
